title: E. Howard Hunt in JFK and Watergate Files
metaDescription: E. Howard Hunt was a longtime CIA officer whose name recurs in JFK assassination files and in post-1972 investigative records from the Watergate break-in.
h1: E. Howard Hunt in JFK files and post-1972 Watergate records
lede: E. Howard Hunt was a longtime CIA officer whose name recurs in both the JFK assassination files and post-1972 investigative records stemming from the Watergate break-in. BlackVaultDocs’ figure hub matches the name E. Howard Hunt in document titles from public NARA releases. The hub is a title index, not a merged biography of two scandals and not a file count. PDFs remain on the originating archive.

sections.h2: What the Hunt figure hub lists
paragraphs: The figure slug e-howard-hunt groups indexed titles that name E. Howard Hunt. The packet supplies no document count, so this page does not invent one. The public-record identity in the blurb is: longtime CIA officer; name recurs in the JFK assassination files and in post-1972 investigative records stemming from the Watergate break-in.

Two series are named: JFK assassination files, and post-1972 investigative records stemming from the Watergate break-in. The packet does not split title hits between those series. This overlay does not invent that split. A title match is a catalog hit, not a finding that the file is an operational cable rather than a later interview.

1972 is the year bound in “post-1972” investigative records in the blurb. The packet does not give a start year for Hunt’s CIA service. This page therefore does not invent one. “Longtime” is the blurb’s word for the length of that service.

sections.h2: JFK files and post-1972 Watergate records as separate series
paragraphs: The blurb says the name recurs in both series. Recurrence is qualitative. This page does not convert it into a count of JFK titles or a count of Watergate titles. Naming both series is a citation of the packet, not an argument that the two episodes are the same investigation.

The related topic href on this packet is the JFK assassination collection. That link is the internal href the packet supplies. Researchers who need the scans should open the originating archive from the figure hub. BlackVaultDocs matches names in titles from public NARA releases; it does not re-host the PDFs.

sections.h2: How name matching works for Hunt
paragraphs: Figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. The Hunt hub is that match, not a complete CIA personnel file and not a complete FOIA log. A missing title hit means the indexed title in this ingest did not match the name as implemented.

The all-figures directory lists other people in the same name index. Use the Hunt hub for titles that name him. Use the collection link for the broader JFK posting named on this packet’s internal links. A Watergate-related title that omits the personal name would not be promised by this name index.

sections.h2: What this page does not claim
paragraphs: This overlay does not argue that Hunt participated in the Kennedy assassination, and it does not retry Watergate. It restates the packet: longtime CIA officer; name recurs in JFK assassination files and in post-1972 investigative records stemming from the Watergate break-in. Conspiracy commentary is outside the index.
No NARA ID is in the facts. No document total is in the facts. Cite post-1972, the JFK assassination files, and the Watergate break-in as named. Do not attach an invented file count to Hunt’s name.

The E. Howard Hunt figure hub is the live title list. All figures shows the rest of the name index. The JFK assassination collection is the related topic link on this packet. Open the originating archive for scans. A later ingest can retag titles; this prose still will not invent a document count.

JFK assassination files and post-1972 Watergate investigative records are two series. Recurrence in both is qualitative. This page does not convert it into two counts. A Watergate title that omits Hunt’s name would not be promised by this name index.

sections.h2: How to cite E. Howard Hunt on this site
paragraphs: Cite E. Howard Hunt as a longtime CIA officer whose name recurs in the JFK assassination files and in post-1972 investigative records stemming from the Watergate break-in, as matched by name in indexed titles on BlackVaultDocs. Do not cite a document count from this guide. Do not treat the figure hub as a finding that joins the two series into one plot. The source note is that figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs.

Cite “longtime CIA officer” as the packet’s length of service; the facts do not give a start year. Cite post-1972 as the year bound on the Watergate series. Cite the JFK assassination files as the other named series. Do not attach a file count to Hunt’s name from this guide.

faqs.q: Who was E. Howard Hunt in the declassified files?
faqs.a: The packet identifies E. Howard Hunt as a longtime CIA officer whose name recurs in the JFK assassination files and in post-1972 investigative records stemming from the Watergate break-in. BlackVaultDocs matches the name in indexed titles. This page does not assign a file count and does not split those two series into totals.

faqs.q: What does post-1972 mean in the Hunt files?
faqs.a: The blurb dates the Watergate-related investigative records as post-1972 records stemming from the Watergate break-in. That is the year bound this page cites. The packet does not give a document count for that series. Titles that name Hunt appear on the figure hub; PDFs remain on the originating archive.

faqs.q: Does Hunt appear in both JFK and Watergate records on this site?
faqs.a: The blurb states that the name recurs in both the JFK assassination files and post-1972 investigative records stemming from the Watergate break-in. It does not count titles in each series. This page does not invent those counts. Open the figure hub and the originating archive for the scans.

faqs.q: Does the Hunt figure hub prove a conspiracy linking JFK and Watergate?
faqs.a: No. The hub matches the name E. Howard Hunt in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. It restates that he was a longtime CIA officer and that the name recurs in both named series. It does not interpret those files as proof of a single plot.

takeaways: E. Howard Hunt was a longtime CIA officer as described in the figure blurb.
His name recurs in the JFK assassination files.
His name also recurs in post-1972 investigative records stemming from the Watergate break-in.
The figure hub matches that name in indexed titles; this packet supplies no document count.
This page does not treat title hits as a finding that joins the two series into one conspiracy.
